newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Peters says NZ dollar has begun to stabilise.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Peters says NZ dollar has begun to stabilise.

text.p: New Zealand Treasurer and Deputy Prime Minister Winston Peters said on Thursday that the New Zealand dollar had begun to stabilise.
"The dollar has begun to stabilise for the first time in a very long time," Peters said in a speech to a business conference in Auckland.
The New Zealand dollar had appreciated by 26 percent in the three year of the previous National government, Peters said.
"It has shown no such indication under a (National-New Zealand First) coalition," he said.
Peters said the balance of payments deficit had come in much lower than some commentators had said it would.
The Consumer Price Index had dropped to 1.8 percent in the year to March -- within the old zero to two percent target band -- and interest rates had fallen, he noted.
Peters reiterated the March 4 Budget Policy Statement (BPS) forecast that the fiscal surplus for 1997/8 would be "well above NZ$3.0 billion".
The BPS forecast the surplus at NZ$3.275 billion, falling to $2.605 billion in 1998 and then rising to $3.457 billion in 1999/00.
Peters delivers his first budget in June.
